title: torchada makes CUDA source run on MUSA, so verify the dispatched kernel instead of assuming a CUDA tuning result carries over
summary: The plugin imports torchada before torch so that torch.cuda/torch.device are redirected to MUSA, and the platform plugin treats torchada.is_musa_platform() as its primary signal. A CUDA-shaped fast path can therefore be present in the source and still be executed by a different implementation on MUSA; an optimization must be attributed to the kernel that actually ran.

hardware: Moore Threads MUSA GPU; no SKU-specific claim is made here
software: torchada, torch_musa and the pinned MUSA toolchain of that revision
models: Any model whose kernels were tuned on CUDA and then run unchanged on MUSA
conditions: Relevant to any port of a CUDA-only optimization, including fused ops, graph capture and attention backends
Not a claim that a specific CUDA optimization is unavailable on MUSA

claims.description: __init__.py imports torchada before torch, with a comment that this must happen before any torch.device("cuda:X") call because it patches torch.cuda to redirect to MUSA.

musa_platform_plugin() returns the MUSA platform when torchada.is_musa_platform() is true and otherwise falls back to importing torch_musa, so availability of the compat layer is itself part of the runtime identity.

A CUDA-specific optimization can compile and run through the compatibility layer without exercising the kernel its CUDA result was measured on; a gain measured on CUDA is therefore a hypothesis about MUSA, not evidence for it.

recommendations: Record torchada, torch_musa, torch and the MUSA toolkit versions next to every measurement; a different compat-layer revision is a different runtime.
Attribute a gain to a named kernel or graph from a profile, and keep the profile beside the engine-level number.
When porting a CUDA fast path, first prove the target backend is selected (dispatch check), then measure; a fallback path that silently wins is the common false positive.
validation_plan: Profile one steady-state step on MUSA and list the top kernels; confirm the intended kernel names appear rather than generic or fallback ones.
Compare against the same step with the candidate disabled, holding device, dtype, shapes and warmup identical.
Re-run the A/B after pinning the compat-layer versions to show the result is not version drift.
limitations: Source-derived reading; no MUSA hardware measurement backed this record.
Kernel names and dispatch rules depend on the exact torchada/torch_musa/plugin tuple.
This record does not name which CUDA optimizations do or do not exist on MUSA.
